newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond trade ideas-dollar and cross mkt switches.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond trade ideas-dollar and cross mkt switches.

text.p: Eurobond analysts' latest trade recommendations focused on dollars, yen and cross market switches.
In eurodollars, Tokyo-Mitsubishi believe that the low amount of 10-year Treasury supply (which is set to continue) is bullish for supranational and sovereign spreads.
They recommend buying the Asian Development Bank 6.75 percent bond, due June 2007 and the 6.75 percent 2007 bond issued by Japan Finance Corp for Municipal Enterprises.
Following are latest trade ideas, compiled by Reuters:
STRATEGY all the above switches result in attractive pick-up's in yield.

A move out of the TEPCO 2003 bond and into the TEPCO 2007 bond provides the largest pick-up of 42 b.p. whilst a switch out of the 6.75 percent NTT 2002 bond or the 7.0 percent JDB 2002 bond into the 6.75 percent JFM 2007 bond delivers a yield pick-up of 32 b.p. and 26 b.p. respectively.

STRATEGY SNCF is a rare Euromarket borrower and is a state entity rather than a corporate. It has a split Moody's rating of AAA/Aa1 to reflect the opinion of long-term risk of privatisation. CADES which is a vehicle for refunding the accumulated defecits of the French social security fund in the 1990's has no privatisation risk and a rating of AAA/AAA by S&P and Moody's reflects this.
The switch results in a 22 b.p. pick-up in yield.

STRATEGY If the third stage of EMU takes place, both bonds will become fungible paying coupon and principle in the euro. In this event the yield of both bonds will converge to parity. The switch at presdent provides a 10 b.p. pick-up in yield.
STRATEGY This switch provides a current yield pick-up of 130 b.p. which is at a three month high.
There is also a wide cost-of-carry between money market rates and the five-year euro. The spread between three-month Libor and the offer side of the Finland 2002 currently stands at 133 b.p.
STRATEGY The shorter end of the euroyen curve should continue to outperform. This switch will give a yield give-up of 75 b.p. against a recent average of 89 b.p.
